verdicts.quote: The bot is a chat page inside a Lightning app that appears in the App Launcher in Lightning Experience ... The bot is offered nowhere else: not in Salesforce Classic, not in the Salesforce mobile app, not in Experience Cloud sites
The callout carries no Salesforce record content, no user name, email or Id, and no org Id or URL, except text the user typed into their message.
The callout carries no Salesforce record content
verdicts.missing: Field-level security is never mentioned; whether the bot's own conversation/message fields (e.g. failure detail, tokens) are FLS-restricted for chat users is undecided.

verdicts.quote: Two permission sets control access: one to chat, one to administer
User B, holding the chat permission set, cannot see user A's conversations or messages ... Only user A, and administrators holding the administer permission set, can.
Salesforce forbids a callout after unsaved database changes in the same request, so the builder must order work so this holds.
verdicts.missing: The callout-after-DML rule is named, but the spec picks a synchronous call (C-20) and leaves it to the builder how to order the DML around the callout. It does not choose a Queueable/future/batch design.

verdicts.quote: The key is not in the deployed source, not in any custom object or setting record, not in any field a user can query ... Searching the debug log of a full chat exchange for the key finds nothing.
Salesforce allows at most 120 seconds for one callout and for all callouts in one request together
verdicts.missing: Callout timeout (120 s) and heap (6 MB, C-29) are given with numbers. CPU time and the callouts-per-transaction count are not.

verdicts.quote: zero real outbound calls (Salesforce forbids callouts in tests, so a simulated xAI is used)
No administrator step to allow the host (such as a Remote Site Setting) is needed beyond what deployment brings.
The runtime does not let the server push partial output to the page during one request, which forces this.
verdicts.missing: The spec relies on the synchronous server call returning the answer inline. It names no platform event, polled status or message channel to tell the interface the answer has arrived.

verdicts.quote: For any failure, the callout log shows exactly one request to xAI for that send. Only the user pressing Send again makes another.

Salesforce refuses the request (for example because the org has too many concurrent long-running requests ...), the panel shows a "could not send, try again" message, re-enables the input and keeps the typed text.
These cases show a message advising the user to try again later: (a) HTTP 429; (b) HTTP 408 or any 500 to 599; (c) the 100-second timeout (C-31)
These cases show a message advising the user to try again later: (a) HTTP 429
If xAI's response reports finish reason "length", the transcript shows the partial text with a visible note stating the answer was shortened

role (user or Grok), text, time sent, order within the conversation, status (success or failed), failure category, HTTP status, failure detail, model used, finish reason, prompt tokens and completion tokens
A conversation, with all its messages, is deleted when its last activity is older than the retention period; default 30 days, allowed 1 to 365
verdicts.missing: What happens to a user's conversations when that user is deactivated or removed is not stated.

verdicts.quote: Each request to Grok carries exactly these items: the system prompt, the history window, the new message, the model name and the reply-length cap ... Nothing else about the user or the org is in the body.

With N = 20, in a conversation of 30 earlier successful messages the request body holds the 20 most recent of them in chronological order ... Older messages remain stored and visible and are not sent.
a message of exactly 4,000 characters can be sent and one of 4,001 cannot
In Setup the administrator changes the model ... or switches the bot off.
An attempt that reaches the callout stage leaves a user message record, and either a Grok answer record, or the user message record marked failed with the category
Secrets do not travel with source deployment, which is why the step exists in every org.
The bot waits up to 100 seconds for Grok's answer and then gives up with a timeout failure
A user opening the app for the first time sees no messages and an invitation to type.
every pre-existing profile, permission set, standard and custom object and field, flow, Apex class, trigger, page and setting is unchanged
